Curated Destination

North India

North India is a land of contrasts, where the bustling streets of Delhi meet the serenity of the Himalayas.

Witness the timeless beauty of the Taj Mahal in Agra, the royal splendor of Jaipur's palaces, and the spiritual energy of the Ganges in Varanasi.

From the snow-capped peaks of Ladakh to the lush valleys of Kashmir, North India offers some of the most dramatic landscapes in the subcontinent.

Places in North India

Place

New and Old Delhi

Delhi is a city of contrasts, where centuries of history unfold alongside the energy and elegance of modern India. Exploring Old Delhi is an immersion into the sights, sounds and aromas of the Mughal capital. A ride on the Rickshaw through the lively lanes of Chandni Chowk, where spice merchants, traditional shops and street-food stalls bring the old city vividly to life. Visit the magnificent Jama Masjid and the imposing Red Fort, reminders of the grandeur of the Mughal emperors, and discover quiet corners where layers of Delhi’s past remain woven into everyday life. A short distance away, New Delhi presents a very different character. Planned during the British Raj, its broad tree-lined avenues, elegant colonial buildings and formal gardens reflect the ambitions of the imperial capital. Highlights include India Gate, the impressive government buildings around Raisina Hill and the atmospheric avenues of Lutyens’ Delhi. Together, Old and New Delhi offer a fascinating introduction to India: a city where Mughal splendour, colonial history and contemporary life exist side by side. It is this remarkable mixture of heritage, colour and everyday energy that makes Delhi such a compelling beginning to a journey through India.

Place

Mumbai

At the edge of the Arabian Sea, grand Victorian buildings, elegant Art Deco architecture and bustling markets unfold alongside contemporary galleries, celebrated restaurants and some of India’s finest hotels. It is a city of contrasts, where the glamour of South Mumbai meets the energy of neighbourhood life and the rhythm of the harbour. Its British legacy is particularly evocative. The grand civic buildings, railway stations and leafy avenues of the former Bombay reveal the ambition of the colonial city, while the Gateway of India stands above the waterfront as a reminder of the port’s place in Britain’s maritime world. Yet Mumbai has never been defined by its colonial past. Indian merchants, artists, filmmakers, workers and entrepreneurs have continually reshaped the city, creating the extraordinary cultural richness found today. For the discerning traveller, Mumbai is best experienced through its atmosphere: an early-morning walk through historic streets, a glimpse of the famous dabbawalas at work, sunset beside the Arabian Sea, or an evening discovering the city’s remarkable culinary scene. Sophisticated, spirited and wonderfully unpredictable, Mumbai is a compelling introduction to modern India.
